(1) species assemblages are identifiable in reef fishes from the Gulf ofMexico, and (2) species assemblage membership is not strongly influenced by life history or productivity.

the application of multivariate statistical analyses to identify species complexes that could be managed as units.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no stock complexes that can be identified with certainty.
the Gulf of Mexico reef fish complex is not a unitary stock.
the Gulf of Mexico reef fish complex concept is a viable approach for managing stocks that lack sufficient data for formal stock assessment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Gulf of Mexico reef fish assemblages can be grouped into 12 complexes that are useful for fisheries management.
species with similar life histories and ecological roles tend to cluster together.
the assemblage approach is a viable option for managing stocks in the absence of a formal assessment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of stock complexes for fisheries management is feasible and may be useful for data-poor species.
the use of stock complexes for data-limited stocks is a reasonable management approach that can be applied in the Gulf of America and other regions.
